home.lede: Read the sacred text while a map travels with you, showing where each passage unfolds in its real setting.
home.seasonLede: Reading plans and map routes to walk this season of the Church.

now.title: What you'll find today
now.body: The 73 books of the Catholic canon in three public-domain versions — Biblia Platense (Straubinger), Catholic Public Domain Version and the Latin Vulgate, with verse-by-verse compared reading. An interactive map with 1,335 places synchronized with the text, historical layers by era, map routes with readings at every stop, global search, reading plans (long journeys, and short ones for what you may be going through), read-aloud, and with your account: bookmarks, highlights and personal notes.

rigor.title: Doctrinal rigor
rigor.body: Only approved versions and verified notes.

calm.title: Aesthetic calm
calm.body: No ads, no gamification, no dark patterns.

privacy.title: Privacy by design
privacy.body: Your data is yours. Optional account, anonymous telemetry.

situations.title: For what you are going through
situations.lede: Plans of three to seven days, with short passages, for a particular moment. They are no substitute for professional help or for the care of someone who knows you.

auth.title: Your Tabor account
auth.lede: With an account, your bookmarks follow you on any device. Reading doesn't require one: it's optional.

plans.title: Reading plans
plans.lede: To read the Bible steadily: long journeys through a book or through a season of the Church, and short plans for what you are going through. Progress is saved on this device.

itineraries.title: Journeys
itineraries.lede: Weeks or months at a time: a whole book, a part of the canon, or the course of a liturgical season.

situations.title: For what you are going through
situations.lede: A few days of reading for a particular moment: a wait, a loss, a decision, a rest.

plans.pastoralNote: These plans keep you company as you read; they are no substitute for professional help or for the care of a priest or someone who knows you. If what you are going through is too heavy to carry alone, find someone you trust and tell them.

visit.title: Places you can visit
visit.metaTitle: Biblical places you can still visit
visit.metaDescription: Guides to the places the Bible names that can still be seen: what survives, where it is, and which passage to read there. The Holy Land first, Paul next.
visit.lede: Many of the places the Bible names are still there. These guides gather the ones you can see today: what survives at each, where it is, and the passage to read while standing there.
visit.sourceNote: Coordinates come from the open atlas at OpenBible.info. What survives at each site, and the passage to read there, are an editorial proposal by Tabor, open to correction: if you find a mistake, please say so.

tierra-santa.lede: From Jerusalem to Galilee: the places of the Gospel and the Old Testament that are still standing, area by area.
tierra-santa.guideLink: See the Holy Land places you can visit

viajes-de-pablo.name: The journeys of Saint Paul
viajes-de-pablo.lede: Greece, Turkey, Malta and Rome: the cities of Acts and of the letters. In preparation.
viajes-de-pablo.guideLink: See the places of Paul's journeys you can visit

jerusalen.name: Jerusalem and around
jerusalen.lede: The city and what you can walk from it in a morning: the Mount of Olives, the valleys that gird it, and the villages just over the ridge.

judea.name: Bethlehem and the Judean hills
judea.lede: The south: Bethlehem eight kilometres from Jerusalem and, beyond it, Hebron and the hill country dropping away towards the desert.

jordan.name: The Jordan Valley and the Dead Sea
jordan.lede: The rift that splits the country from north to south, far below sea level: Jericho, the river of the baptism, and the far bank with Nebo looking out over the promised land.

galilea.name: Galilee and the lake
galilea.lede: Where most of the Gospel takes place: Nazareth, the villages along the northern shore of the lake, Mount Tabor and the plain of Jezreel.

samaria.name: Samaria and the central highlands
samaria.lede: The road between Jerusalem and Galilee that many cross without stopping: Shechem at the foot of Gerizim, Shiloh, Bethel and the Samaria of the kings of Israel.

costa.name: The coast, Carmel and the plain
costa.lede: The flat strip everyone coming from abroad passed through: Caesarea Maritima, Joppa, the Carmel of Elijah and the Philistine cities to the south.

holyLand.title: Biblical places in the Holy Land you can visit today

holyLand.lede: From Jerusalem to Galilee, the places the Bible names that can still be seen: what is left of each one today, where it is, and the passage to read on the spot.
holyLand.howOrganized: The areas follow the way people travel rather than the order of the canon: a trip to the Holy Land is built around two or three bases —Jerusalem, Galilee, sometimes Bethlehem— and from each you go out to whatever lies near. Within each area, what no one skips comes first.
